objectives: Trace the foundational discoveries of immunology from Jenner to the modern era.
Identify the cells + organs of the immune system.
Apply historical context to modern immunological problems.

slides.title: Birth of immunology: from Jenner to Koch
slides.body:
**Edward Jenner** (1796): cowpox inoculation protected against smallpox — the first vaccine (Latin *vacca* = cow). Empirical observation that milkmaids exposed to cowpox were immune to smallpox; deliberate inoculation of James Phipps with cowpox material. Foundation of vaccinology — though mechanism was unknown for >100 yr.

**Louis Pasteur** (1880s): germ theory + **attenuation** of pathogens for vaccines.
- Chicken cholera vaccine (1879) — accidental attenuation by storage.
- Anthrax vaccine (1881) — heat-attenuated.
- Rabies vaccine (1885) — desiccated spinal-cord material; saved Joseph Meister.
- Showed pathogens could be deliberately weakened → immunity without disease.

**Robert Koch**: bacteriologist; **Koch's postulates** (1884) — criteria establishing a microbe causes a disease:
1. Found in all cases of the disease.
2. Isolable in pure culture.
3. Reproduces disease when inoculated into a susceptible host.
4. Re-isolable from the experimentally infected host.

Discovered *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* (1882) + *Vibrio cholerae* (1884). Nobel 1905.

**Emil von Behring + Shibasaburo Kitasato** (1890): discovered **antitoxin** — passive immunity. Serum from animals immunized against diphtheria or tetanus neutralized toxin when transferred to naïve recipients. Behring won the **first Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine** (1901). Foundation of **serotherapy** + later antibody therapy.

**Paul Ehrlich**: developed quantitative antitoxin standardization (still used today as IU). **Side-chain theory** (1897) — cells display receptors ("side chains") that bind antigen; binding triggers production of soluble side chains = antibodies. The first cellular theory of immunity. Nobel 1908. Also coined *magic bullet* — selective targeting (foundation of chemotherapy + targeted drugs).

**Élie Metchnikoff**: discovered **phagocytosis** (1882) watching starfish larvae engulf splinters. Proposed cellular immunity — macrophages + neutrophils as the body's defense. Shared Nobel 1908 with Ehrlich — uniting humoral (Ehrlich) + cellular (Metchnikoff) immunity, the central tension of early immunology resolved as complementary, not opposing.

By 1910 immunology had: vaccines (Jenner, Pasteur), pathogens identified (Koch), antibodies (Behring, Ehrlich), phagocytes (Metchnikoff) — all empirical, no molecular mechanism.

slides.title: The modern synthesis: clonal selection + MHC + the genetics of recognition
slides.body:
**Frank Macfarlane Burnet — clonal selection theory** (1957; Nobel 1960 with Medawar): the central organizing principle of adaptive immunity.
- Each lymphocyte expresses **a single receptor** with unique specificity.
- The repertoire is generated **before antigen exposure**.
- Antigen **selects** lymphocytes whose receptors bind it; selected clones proliferate.
- **Self-reactive clones are deleted** during development → self-tolerance.
- Memory = expanded clones retained after clearance.

Clonal selection explained: specificity, memory, tolerance, diversity — all from one principle. Foundational; everything since builds on it.

**Peter Medawar — acquired immunological tolerance** (Nobel 1960): experiments on mouse-skin grafts demonstrated tolerance can be **induced** by neonatal exposure to foreign antigens. Predicted by Burnet (1949) → tested by Medawar. Foundation of transplantation immunology + tolerance therapy.

**Susumu Tonegawa — V(D)J recombination** (Nobel 1987): solved the **antibody diversity paradox** (how does a finite genome encode 10¹¹ different antibodies?).
- Antibody genes are **assembled by somatic recombination** of Variable (V), Diversity (D), Joining (J) segments.
- Different V/D/J combinations + junctional diversity + somatic hypermutation → ~10¹¹ unique B-cell receptors.
- T-cell receptors use the same mechanism.
- Only known case of **somatic DNA rearrangement** in vertebrate development.

Discovery resolved Burnet's diversity problem at the molecular level.

**Peter Doherty + Rolf Zinkernagel — MHC restriction** (Nobel 1996): T cells recognize foreign antigen **only when presented on self MHC** ("altered self"). Explained transplant rejection + central organizing principle of T-cell biology. Cytotoxic T cells (CD8) recognize peptide on MHC class I; helper T cells (CD4) recognize peptide on MHC class II. Foundation of antigen presentation + the framework for vaccine design + immunotherapy.

By 2000, immunology had: clonal selection (Burnet), tolerance (Medawar), antibody diversity (Tonegawa), MHC restriction (Doherty + Zinkernagel) — a coherent molecular framework underpinning the modern field.

slides.title: The cells + organs of the immune system
slides.body:
**Primary lymphoid organs** — where lymphocytes develop:
- **Bone marrow**: site of hematopoiesis (HSC → all blood + immune cells). B cells mature here in mammals (chickens have a *bursa* — hence "B"). HSC niche regulated by stromal cells (CXCL12, SCF).
- **Thymus**: T-cell maturation site. Thymocytes undergo **positive selection** (must bind self-MHC) + **negative selection** (excessive self-reactivity → apoptosis). Cortex (immature, double-positive CD4⁺CD8⁺) → medulla (single-positive CD4⁺ or CD8⁺ mature cells exported). **AIRE** (autoimmune regulator) drives ectopic expression of tissue-specific antigens in medullary thymic epithelial cells — critical for central tolerance (mutations → APECED).

**Secondary lymphoid organs** — where lymphocytes encounter antigen:
- **Lymph nodes**: encapsulated structures along lymphatic vessels. T-cell zones (paracortex) + B-cell follicles (cortex with germinal centers during response) + medulla. Filter lymph from peripheral tissues; sites of antigen presentation + clonal expansion.
- **Spleen**: filters blood. White pulp = lymphoid (T + B zones); red pulp = RBC clearance. Marginal zone contains specialized macrophages + B cells responding to blood-borne pathogens.
- **Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT)**: protects mucosal surfaces.
  - **GALT** (gut-associated): Peyer's patches in ileum, isolated lymphoid follicles, appendix; M cells sample lumenal antigen.
  - **BALT** (bronchus-associated): airway tissue.
  - **NALT** (nose-associated): tonsils, adenoids.
- **Skin-associated**: Langerhans cells + dermal DCs sample antigen → migrate to draining LNs.

**Major cell types** (HSC-derived):
- **Myeloid lineage**: neutrophils (most abundant; phagocytosis + NETs), monocytes/macrophages (tissue-resident, phagocytic, antigen presentation), dendritic cells (DCs; antigen-presenting, link innate→adaptive), eosinophils (parasites + allergy), basophils + mast cells (allergy + barrier).
- **Lymphoid lineage**: T cells (αβ + γδ; CD4 helper, CD8 cytotoxic, Treg), B cells (humoral immunity, antibody production), NK cells (innate cytotoxicity), innate lymphoid cells (ILC1/2/3, mucosal sentinels).

**Lymphatic system**: vessels carrying lymph from tissues to nodes → thoracic duct → blood. Recirculates lymphocytes (~1-2% of blood lymphocytes circulate per hour). Antigen + dendritic cells from tissues traffic to nodes; activated lymphocytes egress via thoracic duct to seek tissue antigens.

This architecture — production sites + meeting sites + trafficking — makes the immune system the most distributed + dynamic organ system in the body. Subsequent lessons unpack innate immunity, adaptive immunity, antibodies + MHC, vaccines, autoimmunity, + immunotherapy in detail.

question.question: Reconstruct clonal selection theory from observations
question.goal: Burnet (1957) proposed clonal selection. Given the experimental observations available in 1955, derive the core postulates of the theory.

steps.prompt: Observation: antibodies show exquisite specificity against an enormous range of antigens. What does this imply about receptor diversity?
steps.motivation: Ehrlich's side-chain theory predicted preformed receptors.

acceptedAnswers: a vast preformed repertoire of receptors must exist prior to antigen exposure

steps.reveal: Specificity against ~any conceivable antigen (including synthetic chemicals never seen in nature) requires a pre-existing diverse repertoire. Burnet postulated: each lymphocyte carries one receptor specificity; the body produces ~10⁶-10¹¹ different lymphocytes spanning the repertoire. Antigen does not instruct receptor formation (rejecting Pauling's 1940 template theory) but selects among preformed receptors.

steps.prompt: Observation: a second exposure to the same antigen produces a faster, stronger response (memory). What does this imply about the fate of antigen-selected cells?

acceptedAnswers: selected lymphocytes proliferate (clonal expansion) and persist (memory cells)

hints: Faster + stronger → more cells of the same specificity.
steps.reveal: Burnet postulated **clonal expansion**: antigen-selected clones divide, producing effector cells (short-lived) + memory cells (long-lived). Memory is cellular — populations of expanded clones rather than soluble factors. This unified specificity + memory + adaptive response kinetics in one mechanism.

steps.prompt: Observation: organisms do not normally react to their own tissues, but Medawar showed neonatal exposure to foreign antigen induces lifelong tolerance. What does this imply about handling self-reactive clones?

acceptedAnswers: self-reactive lymphocyte clones are deleted (or inactivated) during development

hints: Tolerance is induced when antigen is present during a critical developmental window.
steps.reveal: Burnet predicted **clonal deletion**: lymphocytes encountering antigen during development are deleted (negative selection). Medawar (1953) confirmed by inducing tolerance via neonatal exposure. Now known to occur in thymus (T cells, with AIRE-driven self-antigen expression) + bone marrow (B cells). Peripheral mechanisms (Tregs, anergy) provide additional layers.

steps.prompt: Combine the postulates into a single sentence.

acceptedAnswers: lymphocytes carry unique receptors generated before antigen; antigen selects clones that expand and persist as memory; self-reactive clones are deleted

steps.reveal: **Clonal selection theory**: a pre-formed diverse repertoire of lymphocytes (each with a unique receptor) is generated independently of antigen; antigen selects clones that bind it, which expand + persist as memory; self-reactive clones are deleted during development. This single framework explains specificity, diversity, memory, + tolerance. All subsequent molecular immunology (V(D)J, AID, thymic selection, germinal centers) refines + extends this theory rather than overturning it. Burnet shared the 1960 Nobel with Medawar.

question.question: Why is Tonegawa's discovery of V(D)J recombination considered the molecular completion of Burnet's clonal selection theory?
options: Tonegawa (Nobel 1987) showed that antibody (and TCR) genes are assembled by **somatic recombination** of separate V, D, J gene segments during lymphocyte development. Combinatorial diversity (~50 V × ~25 D × ~6 J for heavy chains) + junctional diversity (N + P additions by TdT) + somatic hypermutation (AID-driven, in germinal centers) → ~10¹¹ unique BCRs/TCRs from a few hundred germline segments. This solved the **diversity paradox** — how a finite genome encodes a vast pre-formed repertoire — exactly as Burnet's 1957 theory required. Schatz + Baltimore later identified RAG1/2 as the recombinase. Tonegawa converted clonal selection from postulate to molecular mechanism, and remains the only known case of somatic DNA rearrangement in vertebrate biology.
It showed that antibodies are proteins.
It is unrelated to clonal selection.
question.explanation: Tonegawa (Nobel 1987) showed V(D)J somatic recombination produces antibody diversity — solving Burnet's diversity paradox at the molecular level. Combinatorial + junctional diversity + somatic hypermutation generate ~10¹¹ unique receptors from finite germline material. Converted clonal selection from postulate to mechanism. Schatz + Baltimore identified the RAG recombinase. The only known case of somatic DNA rearrangement in vertebrates.

hints: What did Burnet need + Tonegawa supplied?
slides.workedSolution: Tonegawa's V(D)J recombination supplied the molecular mechanism for Burnet's required pre-antigen receptor diversity. Combinatorial + junctional diversity + somatic hypermutation generates ~10¹¹ receptors from ~hundreds of germline segments. Completes Burnet's theory at the molecular level.

question.question: A modern parallel to Jenner
question.prompt: Imagine a research team in 2024 develops an mRNA vaccine against a newly emerged pathogen. Drawing on Jenner (1796), Pasteur (1880s), Behring-Kitasato (1890), Burnet (1957), Tonegawa (1987), + the Karikó-Weissman Nobel 2023, explain how 230 years of immunological discovery converge in this single vaccine. Which historical insights are operational in: (a) selecting the immunogen, (b) measuring antibody response, (c) explaining memory + booster strategy, + (d) anticipating which clones will respond? Why was the field unable to deploy mRNA vaccines in 1996 — what late discoveries (modified nucleosides, lipid nanoparticles) were prerequisites?

question.question: Estimate the theoretical antibody repertoire size from heavy + light V(D)J combinatorial diversity. Use ~50 V_H × 25 D_H × 6 J_H × ~40 V_κ × 5 J_κ. Express the number of combinatorial heavy × light chain pairings (ignoring junctional diversity).
question.hint: Multiply the V, D, J counts for heavy chain by V, J counts for κ light chain.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain how immunology evolved from Jenner's empirical vaccination to a molecular discipline with quantitative theory.
question.rubric: Mentions: Jenner (1796) used cowpox empirically — no theory. Pasteur (1880s) generalized via attenuation. Koch (postulates 1884) established pathogen causation. Behring + Kitasato (1890) discovered antibodies; Ehrlich (side-chain theory, magic bullet, Nobel 1908) gave a cellular theory of receptors; Metchnikoff (phagocytosis, Nobel 1908) added cellular immunity. Burnet (1957, Nobel 1960) unified specificity + memory + tolerance via clonal selection. Medawar (Nobel 1960) confirmed tolerance experimentally. Tonegawa (Nobel 1987) supplied V(D)J recombination as molecular mechanism. Doherty + Zinkernagel (Nobel 1996) added MHC restriction. The field transformed from empirical vaccination + serum therapy to a molecular discipline with single-cell resolution + computational repertoire analysis — yet Jenner's vaccine principle remains operational in every modern vaccine deployed today.
